tier1.text: Each optic nerve carries visual information from the retina, the eye's light-sensing layer, to the brain. It is the second cranial nerve, one of twelve nerves connected to the brain. It begins at the very back of the eye, in a blind spot with no light-sensing cells. The two optic nerves meet at the optic chiasm, where some fibers cross to the other side of the brain.

quotes.quote: Because these axons pass through the retina, there are no photoreceptors at the very back of the eye, where the optic nerve begins. This creates a “blind spot” in the retina, and a corresponding blind spot in our visual field.
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

sentences.text: The two optic nerves meet at the optic chiasm, where some fibers cross to the other side of the brain.

quotes.quote: The optic nerves from both sides enter the cranium through the respective optic canals and meet at the optic chiasm at which fibers sort such that the two halves of the visual field are processed by the opposite sides of the brain.
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

quotes.quote: optic chiasm: decussation point in the visual system at which medial retina fibers cross to the other side of the brain
